summary: Amanda K. Goodman specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf, Luis O. Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr., and holds a teaching position at the University of Toronto.

Amar Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied under Rahul Sankrityayan (1960–1963), doctoral supervisor A. K. Warder (attested 1984), and teachers Bimal Krishna Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, Shoryu Katsura, Masafumi Fujimoto, and Alasdair Urquhart.

Amara Ali works in Indology and linguistics. As of 2026, she is attested as a Lecturer in Urdu at both the University of California, Berkeley and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.

Amaranatha Jha (1897–1955) worked in Indology and other fields. He earned his B.A. from Muir Central College (~1913–1917), where he became Professor of English in 1917, later serving as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (~1938–1947) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948).

Amartya Sen (born 1933) is a scholar in philosophy and other fields who studied at the University of Calcutta and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held posts at Jadavpur, Delhi, and LSE, and became a University Professor at Harvard in ~2004.
Amba Kulkarni works in computational linguistics and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Hyderabad by 2009, where she has served as a professor (attested 2018–2026).

Amber D. Carpenter works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under teachers including M. M. McCabe and Verity Harte. Her appointments include posts at the University of York, University of St Andrews, and an associate professorship at Yale-NUS College.

Amelia Bonea (born 1978) works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Tokyo (~2003–2006) and Heidelberg University (~2007–2012), and became a Senior Lecturer at the University of Manchester in ~2021.

Amelia Hall is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her doctorate from the University of Oxford in 2012. Her appointments include Assistant Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism at Naropa University and online religious studies faculty at Central Michigan University.

Amin Sweeney (1938–2010) worked in linguistics and related fields. He earned his doctorate at the University of London (~1967–1970), taught at the National University of Malaysia (1970–1977), and served as Department Chair and emeritus professor at UC Berkeley.
Amita Chatterjee (born 1950) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She held a post as professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University, where she is attested in 1999 and 2009.
Amod Jayant Lele is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at Harvard University under the doctoral supervision of Parimal G. Patil.

Amrit Madhav Ghatage (1913–2003) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor and Head of Linguistics at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1961–1978) and Vice-President of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1993–2003).

Amrith Krishna works in computational linguistics and Indology. He has held positions at the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur, University of Cambridge, IT University of Copenhagen, Oriflow, Uniphore (attested 2023), and Learno.AI (attested 2024–2025).

Amy Heller (born 1951) is a Tibetologist and historian who earned her Ph.D. from the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Ariane Macdonald. She held appointments at the CNRS, Sapienza University of Rome, SOAS, INALCO, and the University of Bern.

Amy Paris Langenberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She received her Ph.D. from Columbia University and served as assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College (~2014–2020).

Amy Sims Miller works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed an M.A. (1995) and Ph.D. (2004) under David Germano at the University of Virginia, and studied under multiple traditional teachers, including Geshe Jampel Thardo and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

Amy Snyder Ohta works in linguistics and Japanology. She completed studies at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1990 and 1993, and became a professor at the University of Washington in ~1995.

Anagarika Dharmapala (1864–1933) was an active figure in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Educated at S. Thomas' College (~1876–1878) and Royal College, Colombo (~1878–1883), he founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891 and the Maha Bodhi Society of India.

Anagarika Govinda (1898–1985) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar with a doctorate from the University of Freiburg. He taught at Visva-Bharati University (1931–1935) and Patna University (1935–1936), and served as Ācārya of Arya Maitreya Mandala (~1933–1985).
